newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dasa says confident on Eurofighter funding.
newsitem.headline: Dasa says confident on Eurofighter funding.

text.p: Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) said on Sunday it was confident the German government would soon approve funding to move the four-nation Eurofighter military jet into production.

But Dasa chief executive Manfred Bischoff also repeated the company's position that it would stop pre-production work, if the Bonn cabinet does not approve some 23 billion marks for the project before parliment's summer recess.

"I am extremely confident that the government will find a solution before the summer break. Discussions with the policy-makers are making good headway," Bischoff said at a news conference at the Paris airshow.
However, "if there is no decision in the cabinet in July, we will stop pre-production activities," he said.
Bischoff said Dasa was not issuing an ultimatum, although he said Dasa could not continue financing work without firm orders.
"We are spending money without somebody telling us we should do it," he said. "We are the ones under pressure, not the other way around."

He said the Eurofighter -- a four-nation project to build 600 jet fighters -- was important to keep jobs, investment and critical technology in Europe, and would help advance the consolidation of Europe's aerospace industry.
"I can't imagine responsible politicians will sweep these facts under the rug," Bischoff said.

Germany's struggle to close a gaping budget deficit and to qualify for European monetary union has raised concerns about funding its purchase of 180 Eurofighter jets. Britain has already agreed to buy 232 of the aircraft with Italy and Spain buying the balance.
The industrial partners had hoped to get government approvals at the end of last year in order to get first deliveries by the year 2001, in time for first service in 2003.
Eurofighter was developed by Dasa, British Aerospace Plc, Finmeccanica of Italy's Alenia, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (Casa) of Spain.
